text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Hijacked Ethiopian plane crashes with 8 Israelis aboard.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat: Don't declare state.
- Syria accuses Israel of warmongering with Golan expansion plans.
- Swiss may dump Holocaust claims in lap of World Jewish Congress.
- Former Police Minister Moshe Shahal: Police report shows Netanyahu met alleged Russian gangster.
- Palestinian Authority launches campaign against Jewish settlements policy. Among proposals: To file suits abroad against settlers with two passports.
- Treasury asks Knesset not to raise parliamentary salaries by 7 percent.
- Israel Aircraft Industries guards suspected of stealing secret documents from company safes.
- Number of ultra-Orthodox exempted from military service rose in 1996 by 25 percent.
- Communications market in Israel to be opened to free competition in 1999.
- American food concern Congra weighs strategic partnership with companies in Israel.
- Lockwood Green engineering of United States to compete for tender to enlarge Israeli sea ports.
- Bank of Israel governor will announce tomorrow whether the interest rates will fall.
